privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: We believe your data is yours. Here is exactly what we collect and why.
privacy.intro_body: OSRS Events ("the Service") is a fan-made web application. We are committed to protecting your privacy and being transparent about what little data we store. This page explains what information is collected when you use the Service, how it is used, and your rights.
privacy.data_intro: When you log in with Discord, we receive the following information from Discord's OAuth2 API:
privacy.data_discord_id_desc: Your unique Discord identifier. Used to link your account across sessions and to identify you within the game.
privacy.data_username_desc: Your Discord username at the time of login. Displayed on your profile and to other players on shared boards.
privacy.data_avatar_desc: A link to your Discord profile picture. Shown on your profile card and as your token on the game board.
privacy.data_nickname_desc: A custom display name you may set yourself in your profile. Replaces your Discord username wherever your name appears.
privacy.data_progress_desc: Your current tile position, completed tiles, and daily dice roll count on each board you participate in.
privacy.no_collect_body: We intentionally collect as little as possible. The following data is never collected:
privacy.no_analytics: Analytics, page views, or behavioural tracking
privacy.no_sell: Any data sold or shared with third parties for commercial purposes
privacy.storage_body: Your data is stored in a private PostgreSQL database. A JSON Web Token (JWT) is saved in your browser's localStorage to keep you logged in for up to 7 days. This token contains only your user ID and is never shared with third parties. You can clear it at any time by logging out.
privacy.third_party_body: We use one external service as part of the login flow:
privacy.discord_note: Discord is used solely for authentication. Once logged in, we do not send any further data to Discord. Discord may log the OAuth2 authorisation request on their end.
privacy.rights_body: You have the right to access, correct, or delete the data we hold about you at any time. Logging out removes your local session token. To request permanent deletion of your account and all associated data, please contact us.
privacy.rights_contact_body: Send us an email with the subject 'Account deletion request' and we will remove your account and all associated data within a reasonable timeframe.
privacy.changes_body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Significant changes will be announced via our Discord server. Continued use of the Service after changes are posted constitutes your acceptance of the updated policy.

snakes.meta_title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders — Free Board Generator
snakes.meta_desc: Build a free Old School RuneScape Snakes & Ladders board for your clan. Assign OSRS tasks to every tile, roll a daily d6 and track everyone's progress.
snakes.title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders
snakes.lead: A free Snakes & Ladders board built for Old School RuneScape clans. Every tile is an OSRS task — complete it to keep climbing, or hit a snake and slide back down.
snakes.how_title: How an OSRS Snakes & Ladders event works
snakes.how_subtitle: Five steps from an empty board to a clan event that runs itself.
snakes.step1_desc: Pick 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9, name the event, and set the start and end dates.
snakes.step2_desc: Every tile gets an Old School RuneScape task. Search the OSRS Wiki from inside the tile editor and the icon and title fill themselves in.
snakes.step3_desc: Choose which tiles launch a player up the board and which drop them back down. No two boards play the same.
snakes.step4_desc: Open the board to anyone, lock it to your Discord server, or hand out invite links you can revoke.
snakes.step5_desc: Players roll a d6 each day, complete the task they land on and mark the tile off. First to the final tile wins.
snakes.why_title: Why Snakes & Ladders instead of bingo?
snakes.why_body: Bingo rewards whoever grinds the most hours, so the clan's biggest account usually settles it in the first weekend and everyone else stops paying attention. Snakes & Ladders puts a dice roll between a player and their next task. That single change means a casual member can climb past a maxed main, and the event stays live to the final day instead of being decided early.
snakes.sizes_subtitle: Pick the size from how long you want the event to run, not from how big your clan is.
snakes.size_5_desc: A weekend event. A good first run, and enough for a smaller clan.
snakes.size_7_desc: The usual pick. Comfortably fills one to two weeks of play.
snakes.size_9_desc: A month-long clan event, with room for genuine long-grind tasks.
snakes.modes_body: Solo boards give every player their own position and their own daily roll. Team boards give each team one shared position, so the team decides together which task to take on next. Teams can be tied to your Discord server so members are grouped automatically instead of by hand.
snakes.faq_a1: Yes. It is free to use, carries no ads and has no paid tier. Donations only cover hosting.
snakes.faq_q2: Does anyone need to install a plugin?
snakes.faq_a2: No. Players log in with Discord in their browser. There is nothing to download and no game client modification involved.
snakes.faq_a3: Players mark their own tiles complete, the same way most clans already run drop-log events on trust plus screenshots. Automatic RuneLite tracking is on the roadmap but is not live yet.
snakes.faq_q4: How many people can join a board?
snakes.faq_a4: There is no player limit. A board works for a handful of friends or a full clan roster.
snakes.faq_q5: Can I stop random people joining?
snakes.faq_a5: Yes. A board can be open to anyone, restricted to members of a specific Discord server, or invite-only using links and six-character codes that you generate and can revoke.
snakes.faq_q6: How many times can someone roll per day?
snakes.faq_a6: You set the daily roll limit per board, or leave it unlimited for a faster event.
snakes.faq_a7: No. OSRS Events is a fan-made project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Jagex.

clan_events.meta_title: OSRS Clan Events — Free Event Board Platform
clan_events.meta_desc: Run Old School RuneScape clan events for free. Build task boards, group members into teams from your Discord server and track everyone's progress in one place.
clan_events.title: OSRS Clan Events
clan_events.lead: Everything you need to run an Old School RuneScape clan event: board building, Discord-based access, teams and live progress tracking. Free, with no ads.
clan_events.why_body: A clan is at its healthiest when members log in with a reason to. Events give the roster a shared goal, pull semi-inactive members back, and give newer players a way to contribute that does not depend on gear or kill count. The idea was never the hard part — the tracking was. Most clans end up with a spreadsheet nobody updates and a Discord thread of screenshots nobody reads.
clan_events.what_subtitle: The parts of running an event that usually eat an organiser's week.
clan_events.feature_boards_desc: Build a 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9 board and put an OSRS task on every tile, pulled straight from the OSRS Wiki.
clan_events.feature_discord_desc: Lock a board to your clan's Discord server so only members can join. No whitelist to maintain by hand.
clan_events.feature_teams_desc: Split the roster into teams that share one board position, or let everyone play their own board solo.
clan_events.feature_invites_desc: Generate invite links with expiry dates and use limits, and revoke any of them at any time.
clan_events.feature_leaderboard_desc: Every board has a leaderboard, so the clan can see where everyone stands without asking in chat.
clan_events.feature_free_desc: No paid tier, no ads and no player cap. Donations cover hosting.
clan_events.access_subtitle: Set this per board — a public community event and a private clan event can run side by side.
clan_events.access_open_desc: Anyone logged in can join. Best for community-wide or cross-clan events.
clan_events.access_guild_desc: Only members of a specific Discord server can join. The usual choice for a normal clan event.
clan_events.access_invite_desc: Players need a link or six-character code that you generate, limit and revoke.
clan_events.setup_body: Start smaller than you think you should. A 5×5 board over a weekend tells you how your clan actually engages, and costs an afternoon to build. Set a daily roll limit so the event paces itself rather than being finished by Sunday. Write your tasks to be checkable from a screenshot — 'get a Dragon Warhammer' settles cleanly, 'do some slayer' does not. Then post the board link in your Discord and pin it, because the single most common reason a clan event dies is that half the roster never found the link.
clan_events.faq_q1: Do I need to be a clan leader to run an event?
clan_events.faq_a1: No. Anyone can create a board. If you lock it to a Discord server, players just need to be members of that server to join.
clan_events.faq_q2: Can we run more than one event at once?
clan_events.faq_a2: Yes. There is no limit on boards, and each one has its own access rules, teams and leaderboard.
clan_events.faq_q3: Can two clans compete against each other?
clan_events.faq_a3: Yes. Use a team board with one team per clan, or an open board that both rosters can join.
clan_events.faq_q4: What happens when an event ends?
clan_events.faq_a4: The board stays available to read after its end date, so you keep the final standings and can look back at previous events.
clan_events.faq_a5: No. Every feature is free, with no ads and no paid tier. Donations cover hosting.

event_ideas.meta_title: OSRS Clan Event Ideas — 8 Formats Compared
event_ideas.meta_desc: Eight Old School RuneScape clan event ideas compared: what each format rewards, how long to run it, and which clan sizes it actually suits.
event_ideas.title: OSRS Clan Event Ideas
event_ideas.lead: Eight event formats OSRS clans actually run, what each one rewards, and how to pick the one that fits your roster.
event_ideas.intro: The best clan event is the one your members finish. A format that carries a 200-member PvM clan will die quietly in a 15-person social clan, and the reverse is just as true. Below is what each format actually rewards, so you can choose on purpose instead of copying whatever the last clan did.
event_ideas.idea1_desc: Every tile is an OSRS task and players roll a daily d6 to advance. Ladders jump you forward, snakes drop you back. Because a dice roll sits between a player and their next task, hours played matter less than in any other format here — a casual member can genuinely beat a maxed main, which keeps the event competitive to the final day.
event_ideas.idea2_desc: A grid of drop or achievement tiles; teams race to complete rows, columns or the full board. Far and away the most popular OSRS event format, and the most demanding. It rewards raw hours, so a few grinders usually decide it early unless you weight the tiles carefully.
event_ideas.idea3_desc: Pick a boss list and a point value per unique, then let teams log drops for a fixed window. Short, trivial to explain and almost setup-free — but it heavily favours whoever can commit the whole weekend.
event_ideas.idea4_desc: Everyone starts from their current XP in a chosen skill and races for the biggest gain. Fair by construction, because it measures change rather than total: a level 60 and a level 99 compete on equal terms.
event_ideas.idea5_desc: Post a fixed set of encounters and let members submit times. It runs indefinitely with no end date, which makes it the lowest-maintenance option on this list — good as a permanent background event between bigger ones.
event_ideas.idea6_desc: Points for diary tiers or quests completed inside the event window. One of the few formats where newer accounts have the advantage, since veterans have already finished everything. Excellent for onboarding a wave of new members.
event_ideas.idea7_desc: Each team hides ships on a grid and fires by completing tasks. Very social and very chat-heavy, but it needs an organiser watching it daily — the format lives or dies on somebody refereeing it.
event_ideas.idea8_meta: Long-term clans · a month or more
event_ideas.idea8_desc: Track collection log slots filled across the whole clan against one shared target. Cooperative rather than competitive, which suits clans where a leaderboard would put people off rather than draw them in.
event_ideas.pick_body: Two questions settle it. First: how much time does your median member have — not your most active one? Formats that reward raw hours reward the top ten percent of your roster and quietly tell everybody else not to bother. Second: who is going to run it? Every format above needs somebody approving completions and answering questions daily. If nobody has volunteered for that yet, run a shorter event than the one you want.
event_ideas.supported_body: OSRS Events currently runs Snakes & Ladders boards with OSRS Wiki task integration, Discord-based access control, teams and live leaderboards. Bingo boards are the next event type on the roadmap.
